name: rules_hash.canonical
description: Cross-SDK canonical rules-hash fixture. Both SDKs must derive these exact hashes from these rules. The hash is the policy_version stamped on every audit event and the pin for approvals, so a divergence here is a release blocker, never a known-divergence.

expected.set_hash_note: Order-insensitive over enabled rules; disabled rules excluded.

ordering.note: Rule ids are sorted before hashing, and the two languages sorted DIFFERENTLY: Python by code point, TypeScript by UTF-16 code unit. The orders agree on everything except an ASTRAL id meeting a BMP id in U+E000..U+FFFF, where JS sees the astral character's leading surrogate (U+D800..U+DBFF) and sorts it FIRST while Python sees U+10000+ and sorts it LAST. So the two SDKs stamped a different policy_version on identical policy - and policy_version is inside the chain preimage under format 3, which makes a wrong value durably wrong. This case is here because the rules above use ASCII ids only: they sort identically under both orders and could never have caught it.

resolution_binding.note: A DECLARED conflict-resolution mode is committed into the hash, and the hash then commits to exactly what can change a decision under that mode: first_match hashes the projections in evaluation order (list position decides there), deny_wins sorts them by id (position cannot decide, so a pure reordering keeps the version). Undeclared rulesets keep the historical order-insensitive bytes pinned above, so a deployed fleet never sees its policy_version move under an unchanged policy and a mixed-language fleet never stamps two versions for one policy. The two rules below decide differently by order under first_match - the topic_allow pre-empts the block when listed first - which is exactly why their two orderings must not share a policy_version.

expected.undeclared_hash_note: Identical for both orderings: the historical bytes, preserved.
expected.deny_wins_hash_note: Identical for both orderings: under deny_wins a reorder changes no decision, and the version says so.
